text:
Jun (oncall): noticing provisioning failures in us-west1-ephemeral yesterday, GPU attach failing with iops errors.
Priya: saw alerts — nvme io-latency spiked, janitor throughput had bursts around 02:10 UTC.
Alex: pulling logs from gnode-472, dropping snippet: 
```
nvme0n1: read qdepth 128 inflight 60 latency 35ms
kernel: scrubber: deleting backlog 12k files
iostat -x:
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 10.00 900.00 64.00 9200.00 20.0 1.8 1.95 0.15 2.10 0.35 98.7
```
Maya: that nvme util is basically saturated, GPUs can't claim nodes because attach is waiting on local cleanup.
Jun (oncall): impact: ~120 pending GPU requests queued, median attach latency up to 3.2s, autoscaler decision loops misfiring.
Priya: looks like scrub backlog + a retention snapshot job overlapped, causing the janitor to escalate concurrency.
Alex: short mitigation plan — throttle janitor concurrency to 2 in us-west1 and add backoff after a failure.
Maya: can we divert scheduling of non-urgent preemptible GPU workloads to us-central for the next 2h? cost bump but keeps customer-facing jobs alive.
Jun (oncall): approved. Routing policy updated to prefer us-central for lower-priority preemptible pools.
Alex: applied quick patch to daemonset in us-west1: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/janitor CONCURRENCY=2 --context=us-west1
```
Priya: watching dashboards — nvme util dropped to ~55% after throttle, attach failures decreased. :thumbsup:
Maya: follow-up actions: implement per-node scrub rate limits and a probe that defers janitor work if nvme util > 80%. Also add an alert for scrub bursts correlated with gpu-attach failures.
Jun (oncall): opened follow-up GH ticket GH-5642 for scrub rate controls + canary config.
Alex: will run a 12h canary in us-west1 tonight during the low-traffic window to validate.
infra-bot: created incident INC-2026-0423 and assigned to eng-infra.
Jun (oncall): thanks all — keeping thread open, will post postmortem notes and ETA for the rate-limiter rollout.
